tips: Hi, I'm Kalam! Press ▶ Run to start any program. You can change the code and run it again!
Tip: press Ctrl + Enter to run your code quickly. ⚡
Mistakes are how we learn! If something goes wrong, I'll explain it in simple words. 🤗
Try the 🐢 turtle examples in Python to draw colourful pictures!
Your code is saved automatically in this browser. Use 💾 Save to keep a copy on your computer.
Change one small thing at a time, then press Run. That's how real programmers work! 🧑‍💻

error.title: What went wrong (simple)
error.titleSystem: Hmm, something is in the way

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Read the full error below, or ask your teacher for help. 🤔
errors.timeout: Your program ran for too long — maybe a loop never stops? 🔁
errors.output_limit: Your program printed too much, so we stopped it. Maybe a loop never stops? 🔁
errors.memory: Your program used too much memory. Maybe a list or a loop keeps growing forever? 🐘
errors.rate_limited: Slow down a little! Wait a moment, then press Run again. 🐢
errors.busy: Lots of students are running code right now. Please try again in a few seconds. 🚦
errors.offline: Can't reach the Kalam server. Check the internet connection. (Python works even without internet!) 📡
errors.server_setup: C and C++ can't run on this website yet — the server that builds C programs isn't set up. Please tell your teacher. Python works! 🐍
errors.compiler_load: The C/C++ compiler couldn't be downloaded. Check the internet connection and press Run again. (Python works without it!) 📡
errors.code_too_long: Your program is too long to run here. 📜
errors.python_load: Python couldn't start in this browser. Try reloading the page, or use a newer Chrome, Edge or Firefox. 🔄
errors.py_name_bool: In Python, {{name}} must be written as {{correct}} — with a capital letter at the start. 🔠
errors.py_name_typo: Oops! The computer doesn't know the word '{{name}}'. Did you mean '{{suggestion}}'? 🔍
errors.py_name_quotes: The computer doesn't know '{{name}}'. If you want to show the word {{name}}, put it inside quotes: "{{name}}" ✍️
errors.py_name_undefined: The computer doesn't know the word '{{name}}' yet. Check the spelling, or create it first (like {{name}} = 5) before you use it. 🔍
errors.py_unbound_local: You used '{{name}}' inside a function before giving it a value there. Give it a value first, or pass it into the function. 📦
errors.py_smart_quotes: There are curly “fancy” quotes in your code. Python needs straight quotes like " or '. Type them again using the keyboard. ✍️
errors.py_invalid_char: There is a character Python doesn't understand: {{char}} — delete it and type it again using the keyboard. ⌨️
errors.py_print_parens: print needs round brackets. Write it like this: print("Hello") 🙂
errors.py_else_if: In Python we write elif, not else if. Change it to: elif ... : 🔀
errors.py_missing_colon: A colon (:) is missing at the end of this line. Lines that start with if, elif, else, for, while or def must end with : 🎯
errors.py_assign_in_if: To check if two things are equal, use two equals signs ==. One = is for storing a value. ⚖️
errors.py_never_closed: You opened a bracket {{open}} but never closed it. Add {{close}} in the right place. 🧩
errors.py_unmatched: There is an extra closing bracket {{close}} without an opening one. Remove it, or add the opening bracket. 🧩
errors.py_bracket_mismatch: The brackets don't match: you opened with {{open}} but closed with {{close}}. 🧩
errors.py_unterminated_triple: A text that starts with three quotes """ never ends. Add the closing """ 📝
errors.py_unterminated_string: Your text is missing its closing quote. Every " needs a partner " at the end of the text. 📝
errors.py_expected_indent: The line after a colon (:) must be moved to the right. Press Tab, or add 4 spaces at the start of the line. ➡️
errors.py_unexpected_indent: This line is moved to the right, but it shouldn't be. Remove the extra spaces at the start. ⬅️
errors.py_unindent_mismatch: The spaces at the start of this line don't line up with the lines above. Make them match exactly. 📏
errors.py_tabs_spaces: This code mixes Tabs and spaces at the start of lines. Use only one kind (4 spaces is best). 📏
errors.py_number_name: A name can't start with a number, and a number can't have letters stuck to it. Did you forget * for multiply, like 2*x? 🔢
errors.py_assign_literal: You can't store a value into a number or a text. The name goes on the LEFT, like: score = 10 ⬅️
errors.py_outside_function: '{{word}}' can only be used inside a function (after def). 📦
errors.py_outside_loop: '{{word}}' can only be used inside a loop (for or while). 🔁
errors.py_forgot_comma: It looks like a comma is missing between two things. Example: print("Age:", age) 🧷
errors.py_eof: Python reached the end of your code, but something isn't finished — maybe a missing bracket or quote. 🧩
errors.py_keyword_name: '{{word}}' is a special Python word, so it can't be a name. Try another name like my_{{word}}. 🏷️
errors.py_concat_str_num: You can't join text and a number with +. Turn the number into text with str(), like "Age: " + str(age) — or use a comma inside print. 🔗
errors.py_add_num_str: You're doing maths with text. input() always gives text — turn it into a number with int(...) or float(...). 🔢
errors.py_compare_str_num: You're comparing text with a number. Use int(...) to turn the text into a number first. ⚖️
errors.py_multiply_seq: Text can only be repeated a whole number of times, like "ab" * 3. Did you forget int(...) around input()? ✖️
errors.py_not_callable: Something that is not a function is used with brackets ( ). Did you forget * for multiply, like 2*(3+4)? 🤔
errors.py_not_callable_shadow: You used the name '{{name}}' for a variable, so the computer forgot it was a command. Choose a different variable name. 🏷️
errors.py_missing_arg: The function {{func}}() needs {{count}} more value(s) inside its brackets. 📦
errors.py_too_many_args: The function {{func}}() wants {{expected}} value(s), but you gave {{given}}. ✋
errors.py_not_iterable: You can't loop over a single number. To count, use range(), like: for i in range(10): 🔁
errors.py_not_subscriptable: You used [ ] on a {{type}}, but [ ] only works on lists and text. 📋
errors.py_index_type: The position inside [ ] must be a whole number. If it came from input(), use int(...). 🔢
errors.py_none_type: Something has no value (None). Maybe a function is missing 'return', or a variable was never set. 🕳️
errors.py_int_conversion: You typed '{{typed}}', but the program needs a whole number like 7. Run again and type digits only. 🔢
errors.py_int_conversion_decimal: You typed '{{typed}}' — that has a decimal point, but int() needs a whole number. Type a number like 7, or use float() in the code. 🔢
errors.py_int_conversion_empty: You pressed Enter without typing anything. The program needs a number — run again and type one. ⌨️
errors.py_float_conversion: You typed '{{typed}}', but the program needs a number like 3.5. Run again and type a number. 🔢
errors.py_zero_division: You tried to divide by zero — even computers can't do that! Check the number you are dividing by. ➗
errors.py_index_range: You asked for an item that isn't there. Remember: a {{kind}} with 3 items has positions 0, 1 and 2. 📋
errors.py_key_error: The dictionary has no key called {{key}}. Check the spelling. 🔑
errors.py_attribute_nosuggest: '{{owner}}' doesn't have anything called '{{attr}}'. Check the spelling. 🔍
errors.py_module_missing: The module '{{module}}' isn't available here. Check the spelling. You can use random, math, time, turtle and other built-in modules. 📦
errors.py_import_name: That name can't be imported from '{{module}}'. Check the spelling. 📦
errors.py_recursion: A function kept calling itself again and again. Make sure it has a stopping condition. 🔁
errors.py_overflow: The number got too big for the computer to handle. 🐘
errors.py_turtle_color: The turtle doesn't know that colour. Try a name like "red" or "blue". 🎨
errors.py_value_unpack: The number of names on the left doesn't match the number of values on the right. ⚖️
errors.py_no_input: This program wants you to type an answer, but this page can't wait for typing yet. Please reload the page (Ctrl + Shift + R) and run again. If it keeps happening, tell your teacher. 🔄
errors.py_eof_input: The program wanted more typing, but nothing was given. ⌨️
errors.py_generic_syntax: Python couldn't understand this line. Look carefully for missing brackets, quotes, colons or commas. 🔍
errors.py_generic_type: Two kinds of things are used together that don't mix (like text and numbers). 🧪
errors.py_generic_value: A value wasn't right for what the program tried to do. 🤔
errors.c_missing_semicolon: A semicolon ; is missing. In C and C++, most lines must end with ; — check the end of this line (or the line just above). ✏️
errors.c_std_missing: The computer doesn't know '{{name}}'. Add  using namespace std;  below your #include lines, or write std::{{name}}. 📚
errors.c_cpp_missing_include: To use '{{name}}', add  #include <{{header}}>  at the top of your program. 📚
errors.c_implicit_function_header: To use {{name}}(), add  #include <{{header}}>  at the top of your program. 📚
errors.c_name_typo: Oops! The computer doesn't know the word '{{name}}'. Did you mean '{{suggestion}}'? 🔍
errors.c_undeclared: The computer doesn't know '{{name}}'. Check the spelling, or create it first, like: int {{name}} = 0; 📦
errors.c_bad_header: There is no library called '{{header}}'. Did you mean <{{suggestion}}>? 📚
errors.c_bad_header_nosuggest: There is no library called '{{header}}'. Check the spelling. 📚
errors.c_include_syntax: The #include line is written wrongly. It should look like: #include <stdio.h> 📚
errors.c_unknown_type: The computer doesn't know the type '{{name}}'. Check the spelling (int, float, double, char). 🏷️
errors.c_unknown_type_string: C has no 'string' type. Use a character array like  char name[50];  (or switch to C++). 🔤
errors.c_unknown_type_bool: To use bool in C, add  #include <stdbool.h>  at the top. ✅
errors.c_missing_brace_end: A closing curly bracket } is missing. Every { needs a partner }. 🧩
errors.c_missing_paren: A closing round bracket ) is missing on this line. 🧩
errors.c_unterminated_string: A text is missing its closing quote ". 📝
errors.c_stray_char: There is a strange character in your code (often curly quotes “ ” copied from a document). Type the quotes again using the keyboard. ✍️
errors.c_main_missing: Every C/C++ program needs a main function:  int main() { ... }  Check that it's spelled correctly. 🏠
errors.c_undefined_reference: The function '{{name}}' is used but never written. Check its spelling. 🔍
errors.c_else_without_if: This 'else' has no 'if' before it. Check for an extra ; after if (...), or a missing }. 🔀
errors.c_break_outside: 'break' and 'continue' can only be used inside a loop or a switch. 🔁
errors.c_lvalue: The left side of = must be a variable name. To compare two things, use == ⚖️
errors.c_redefinition: '{{name}}' was created twice. Give each variable or function its own name. 🏷️
errors.c_too_few_args: The function {{func}}() needs more values inside its brackets. 📦
errors.c_too_many_args: The function {{func}}() was given too many values. ✋
errors.c_void_value: A void function doesn't give back a value, so you can't use its result here. 🕳️
errors.c_return_no_value: This function must give back a value, like: return 0; ↩️
errors.c_type_mismatch: You're mixing types that don't fit together (like text and a number). Check the types of your variables. 🧪
errors.c_invalid_operands: These two things can't be used together with this sign. 🧪
errors.c_cin_cout_arrows: The arrows point the wrong way! Use  cin >> x  to read and  cout << x  to print. ↔️
errors.c_subscript: [ ] can only be used with arrays, and this variable isn't an array. 📋
errors.c_member_access: That variable doesn't have a part with that name. Check the spelling after the dot. 🔍
errors.c_case_outside: 'case' and 'default' must be inside a switch block. 🔀
errors.c_duplicate_case: Two 'case' labels have the same value. Each case must be different. 🔀
errors.c_jump_case: In C++, put { } around a case that creates a new variable. 🧩
errors.c_expected_expression: Something is missing here — maybe a number, a variable or a bracket. 🔍
errors.c_expected_identifier: The computer expected a name here. Check for extra or missing symbols. 🔍
errors.c_does_not_name_type: '{{name}}' isn't a type the computer knows. Check the spelling, and that your code is inside main(). 🏷️
errors.c_main_return_type: main must be written as:  int main()  🏠
errors.c_string_literal_char: Single quotes ' ' hold only one character. For words, use double quotes " ". 🔤
errors.c_segfault: Your program crashed 💥 It probably used a memory place it shouldn't — like going past the end of an array, or forgetting & in scanf: scanf("%d", &x).
errors.c_div_zero: Your program divided by zero — even computers can't do that! ➗
errors.c_out_of_range: Your program asked for a position that doesn't exist (like item 10 in a list of 5). 📋
errors.c_invalid_argument: Some text couldn't be turned into a number. Check what was typed. 🔢
errors.c_abort: Your program crashed and had to stop 💥 Common reasons: dividing by zero, using a position outside an array, a function that forgot to return a value, or using too much memory.
errors.c_exit_code: Your program finished with code {{code}}. Usually main should end with  return 0;  ↩️
errors.c_generic_compile: The compiler found a problem on this line. Look carefully for a missing ; bracket, or a spelling mistake. 🔍
errors.w_scanf_ampersand: Did you forget & in scanf? Write scanf("%d", &x) so the answer goes into x.
errors.w_assign_in_if: Inside if ( ), use == to compare. A single = changes the value!
errors.w_format_type: The % code doesn't match the variable type (%d for int, %f for float, %lf for double in scanf, %c for char, %s for text).
errors.w_no_return: This function might end without giving back a value. Add a return line.
errors.w_uninitialized: '{{name}}' is used before it gets a value. Give it a starting value, like  int {{name}} = 0;
